summary: Repair current person routing with st persons rename OLD NEW --as OLD_OR_NEW --idempotency-key KEY or POST /v1/persons/rename: move eligible open person steps and pending human reviews once, preserve history and declarations, and report everything still naming OLD that needs attention.

replay.detail: The new durable work.person-reassigned, gate.reviewer-reassigned and person.rename.completed claim kinds preserve current routing and the completed repair receipt across reopen, replication and graph replay. Existing historical actors, original requests, answered review history, run requesters and saved mission/run specifications are not rewritten. No automatic historical identity migration or alias is installed; additive report fields default to empty when reading older completion receipts. Ordinary upgrade does not request a full historical replay.

schema.detail: Adds registered claim shapes for work.person-reassigned, gate.reviewer-reassigned and person.rename.completed, plus SQLite human-gate request, episode, reassignment and answer indexes used by pending-review reads. Global attention reads seek review candidates from open mission, step and loop owners instead of enumerating historical requests across the store. Candidate-first hydration uses exact claim-ID seeks so SQLite cannot reorder it into a scan of unrelated indexed review history. These reads exclude answered or superseded requests before hydration. Unresolved candidates are materialized before looking up the first request in each episode, so answered history does not incur discarded episode sorts; waiting-since timestamps and canonical ordering are preserved. Exact-request joins remove SQLite column affinity so JSON request IDs seek the expression indexes instead of scanning unrelated episodes. The database schema version is unchanged; indexes are installed on store open. No destructive table conversion is required.

rules.detail: All three repair claim kinds are durable in the retention manifest: reassignment evidence and completed receipts are not an expiring alias or temporary overlay. The retention manifest changes the checkpoint rules digest even though the numeric rules version is unchanged. Upgrade every participating member before invoking repair; mixed builds do not share the same retention digest and older members do not understand the new claims. Do not rely on mixed-build checkpoint progress or review-routing agreement.

compatibility.detail: Adds the persons rename CLI and POST /v1/persons/rename without legacy aliases. OLD and NEW must be distinct complete person subjects, the actor must be OLD or NEW (agents and unrelated people are refused), and NEW must already be known from stored identity or routing evidence. PersonRenameReport retains reassigned_steps, reassigned_reviews, run_requesters, missions_to_republish and namespace_notice, and adds defaulted unchanged_attention_requests, unchanged_fault_cards, unchanged_revision_approvals, unchanged_planning_launch_approvals, live_run_references and published_mission_references. The unchanged lists identify current items not moved; fault cards use episode claim IDs. The reference maps identify precise JSON-pointer routing paths in live-run retained specs, current-generation runtime assignees and published missions. Runtime assignees use /step_runs/<escaped-step-subject>/assignee separately from saved-spec routes and /requester. Older receipts remain readable, but older binaries/clients cannot be assumed to apply repair routing or expose these new report categories. No cross-version client compatibility proof is claimed. Client-derived custom/person namespaces, private glasses and terminals are not migrated.

downtime.detail: Deploying the compatible build requires normal member restarts; restart-to-API and restart-to-health timing for this change have not been measured. The repair uses one writer transaction for its fence, routing writes and receipt; do not assume it is free of writer contention on a large store.

manual.detail: Upgrade all fleet members, ensure NEW is already known, and submit the repair through one member using a retained explicit idempotency key. Save the full JSON report. Inspect every unchanged attention request, fault card, revision approval and planning-launch approval. Inspect all live_run_references and published_mission_references: update and republish declaration sources for future work, use the authorized run-revision workflow where appropriate for live work, and retain immutable specifications and historical requester attribution. Publishing alone does not revise an existing run. The completed receipt fences OLD against a different destination with person-rename-conflict before any routing writes on that member, preventing competing local OLD-to-A and OLD-to-B requests from splitting the repair. Disconnected members may each initially accept different destinations. After receipts replicate, the earliest completed receipt per OLD in canonical claim order, including envelope ordering, selects one destination consistently for work and review routing. This is eventual convergence, not global admission exclusion before replication; use one member rather than deliberately issuing competing requests. See docs/missions-in-practice.md.

recovery.detail: After a lost response, retry the identical OLD, NEW, actor and idempotency key through the same upgraded member; the winning committed receipt returns its original report after reopen or replication, while an uncommitted transaction leaves no partial routing writes. Reusing the key for another request returns idempotency-conflict. A retry is not a fresh sweep of later work. If disconnected members accepted competing repairs, exchanged receipts select the canonical-earliest winner and rebuild affected run projections to remove losing work and review routes. Retrying a losing receipt's exact request returns person-rename-conflict rather than its earlier report; the winning exact retry remains write-free. Inspect the winning receipt and roll forward rather than attempting another destination or deleting receipt claims. Keep all members on compatible builds after writing repair claims. Reinstalling an older binary does not undo durable routing claims or restore old-reader compatibility. A rollback requiring pre-repair state needs a coordinated fleet restore from a pre-repair backup and loses subsequent claims; do not restore only one member into a live fleet. Finish handling unchanged items and republishing corrected declarations as the normal recovery path.
